findings.rationale: Both recursive expression transformers fall through on Expr::Stage even though the shared child visitor treats its entity as a child. Predicate calls under stage therefore survive expansion, and refinement substitutions under stage are silently skipped.

Inlining checks whether binders inside the definition capture argument variables, but does not protect free variables in the definition body from an enclosing binder at the call site. A predicate referring to global x, called beneath a binder also named x, is rewritten with different semantics.

Pre-expansion reserved-name validation covers only definition names and parameters. Reserved binder names or other local declarations in an unused definition disappear when definitions are removed and consequently evade the later model-wide check; acceptance therefore depends on whether the definition is referenced.

with_origin unconditionally replaces an existing precise diagnostic origin, including with None, while Display never falls back to ModelError.span. The state and struct resolution wrappers can therefore erase conditional-expression locations, and direct-source errors recorded only through at() render without any location.

Struct fields are resolved directly into a Vec without checking field-name uniqueness. A duplicate declaration is accepted, while default construction collects fields into a BTreeMap and silently overwrites one entry, leaving the declared type and runtime value shape inconsistent.

Domain and TypeRef range construction never rejects lo greater than hi, and static leadsTo expansion likewise turns such a range into zero bindings. Invalid state types can receive defaults outside their enumerated domain, while liveness obligations over reversed binders can disappear vacuously; action ranges already reject this condition.

Only actions maintain a name set. Duplicate invariant, transition, reachable, and leadsTo names are accepted despite sharing the same property target for origins and annotations, and repeated terminal declarations silently overwrite the earlier expression. Diagnostics and metadata can consequently refer to a different declaration than the evaluated one.

Duplicate-write analysis resolves every variable index against global constants and enum members without removing names shadowed by action parameters, lets, or loop binders. It can incorrectly prove two indices distinct and allow two writes to the same runtime location.

Division and remainder guard zero but not the signed overflow case i64::MIN with -1. div_euclid and rem_euclid can panic for that valid input expression instead of returning ModelError, allowing source-controlled constants to terminate model construction.
